sections.h2: What are your choices for selling a house in Bay City?
sections.html:
Bay City sellers can list on the open market, handle a sale themselves, or take a cash purchase from a buyer who accepts the property in its present condition. All three finish with a recorded deed and Michigan transfer tax, so the real decision is how much time, repair work and uncertainty you want to carry.

An older house near the river often needs the most thought. Many Bay City homes date from the lumber era, and a buyer using a mortgage will usually order an inspection that turns up wiring, roofing or foundation items. A cash buyer prices those in and skips the repair negotiation.

  • Listing: widest exposure, longest timeline, repair requests likely.
  • For-sale-by-owner: no listing commission, but you manage the contract and disclosures.
  • Cash sale: simpler closing, price set by the condition of the house.

sections.h2: What should a seller know about Bay City itself?
sections.html:
Bay City is the Bay County seat, set on the Saginaw River just upstream from Saginaw Bay, with about 10 square miles of land. West Bay City, on the river's west bank, was a separate city until it was annexed in 1905, and several bridges still link the two sides. The Center Avenue Historic District holds more than 250 buildings on the National Register, many of them lumber-boom houses, and Midland Street and Water Street (home to a large antique district) anchor the older commercial areas.

The job base is a mix of health care, schools and industry. The city's financial report lists McLaren Bay Region (about 1,880 employees), Bay City Public Schools (792), Bay County (589), S. C. Johnson and Son (450) and General Motors Powertrain (432) among the top employers, and Michigan Sugar is also based here. Highways include I-75, US 10, M-13 and M-25.

The river brings an advantage and a caution. Waterfront and historic-district houses draw a particular kind of buyer, while the region's humid continental climate means cold winters that expose weak roofs and old heating systems.

sections.h2: Which Bay City neighborhoods and schools shape buyer interest?
sections.html:
Bay City Public Schools runs three high schools, Central, Western and Eastern, along with two middle schools and seven elementary schools, so a house's attendance zone is a real selling point. List the zone clearly when you advertise.

The city is organized around several business corridors. Downtown sits between Madison Avenue and the Saginaw River, the Banks district runs along Marquette Avenue, and the Broadway, Columbus and Johnson Street districts serve the surrounding blocks. Industrial pockets along Morton Street, Harrison Street, Woodside Avenue and the Marquette Industrial Center sit close to some of the older housing, which can affect noise and traffic for a buyer.

  • West Bay City on the west bank was its own city until the 1905 annexation.
  • The Center Avenue Historic District favors buyers who value large period houses and accept upkeep.
  • The Columbus Avenue business district runs out toward Bay Medical Center Hospital.

Match your marketing to the block. A cash buyer looks at condition first, while a retail buyer weighs school zone, commute and character.

sections.h2: Do Bay City rental rules affect a sale?
sections.html:
Yes, if the house has tenants or could be rented. The city requires every rental property to be registered, inspected and certified before a tenant occupies it, and the city's rental page carries the registration forms and a tenant complaint form. A rental that was never registered can come to light when a code officer visits, and that is better dealt with before a buyer's inspector finds it.

If you are selling a rental, gather the registration, the certification and any inspection correction letters. A buyer who plans to keep the tenants will want them, and a buyer who plans to live there will want to know the units are legal.

Utilities add one local wrinkle. Bay City runs its own utility billing, and trash charges are placed on electric accounts for occupied and unoccupied homes alike. Settle the final bills and ask Utility Customer Service at 989-894-8104 about closing out the accounts at the transfer.

sections.h2: How much does recording a deed in Bay County cost?
sections.html:
The Bay County Register of Deeds charges a flat $30 for each deed, mortgage or other instrument regardless of page count, and $4 of that goes to the state survey and remonumentation fund. Warranty deeds, land contracts and condominium master deeds also need a tax certificate from the Bay County Treasurer, which costs $5 on a separate check.

Transfer tax is set by two statutes. The county's schedule lists the state tax at $7.50 and the county tax at $1.10 per thousand dollars of consideration, which together equal $8.60 per $1,000. On a $100,000 sale the total is $860.

The deed must state the full consideration or carry a transfer affidavit, and any exemption has to be written on the face of the instrument. Exempt transfers under the state act include a deed from a parent to a child and a deed given in foreclosure.

sections.h2: How are Bay City property taxes handled when I sell?
sections.html:
The City Treasurer collects taxes first. Beginning March 1, unpaid residential taxes go to the Bay County Treasurer at 515 Center Avenue (989-895-4285), where interest and fees increase. Ask the title company to confirm both summer and winter bills are paid or prorated before the deed is recorded.

Michigan's statewide summer deadline is September 14, but city charters may set different dates, so confirm Bay City's with the Treasurer. Late summer payments add 1% a month under the state schedule, and an unpaid balance returns to the county on March 1.

If you claimed a principal residence exemption, file the rescind form with the city assessor within 90 days of leaving the home. The city assessor can supply the form.

sections.h2: How can you compare a cash offer with a listing?
sections.html:
Work out your likely net on each path. For a listing, subtract agent fees, repairs the buyer's inspection will request, transfer tax, and carrying costs for the months you wait. For a cash offer, subtract only what the buyer says you will pay, then confirm that in writing.

Ask any buyer who covers title and recording, whether the offer can change after a walk-through, and what closing date is firm. A reputable buyer will answer without pressure and will let you take time to compare.

faqs.q: Can I sell my Bay City house if it needs major repairs?
faqs.a: Yes. A cash buyer purchases a house as-is and prices the repairs into the offer, and you can also list it at a lower price and disclose known defects. Weigh the repair estimate against the median Bay City home value of $97,600 before spending money on renovation.

faqs.q: How much is transfer tax on a Bay City home sale?
faqs.a: The Bay County schedule puts state tax at $7.50 and county tax at $1.10 per $1,000, for $8.60 per $1,000 in all. A $90,000 sale would carry $774 in transfer tax, paid by the seller unless the contract says otherwise.

faqs.q: Do I have to register my rental house before selling it in Bay City?
faqs.a: The city requires registration, inspection and certification before a tenant occupies a rental. If your house has been rented, collect the paperwork now, because buyers and title companies may ask for it.

faqs.q: Who do I pay property taxes to if I sell after March 1?
faqs.a: Unpaid residential taxes are payable to the Bay County Treasurer starting March 1. Settle the balance with the county treasurer or through the closing so the buyer receives a clean title.

faqs.q: How long does it take to record a deed in Bay County?
faqs.a: The Register of Deeds records documents that meet its requirements and returns any that do not. Your title company normally submits the deed right after closing, so ask them for the recording confirmation date.
